This first bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.58 of 2023 registered at Police Station Sumavali, District Morena (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(D),
376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 09-08-2023.

As per the case of prosecution, father of prosecutrix reported to Police Station Somavali, District Neetesh Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58441716/
1 Morena on 03-06-2023 that his daughter aged around 13 years is missing since night of 02-06-2023.

sentences.text: He suspected that Vinod Kushwah has allured and taken his daughter.
On such allegations, PS Somavali registered FIR at Crime No.58 of 2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against Vinod Kushwah.
During enquiry, victim was recovered from Saharanpur (UP) on 03-07-2023.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, victim stated that she desires to marry to Vinod Kushwah, therefore, she had called Vinod Kushwah.
Vinod Kushwah refused to take her along with him.
She tried to threaten Vinod.
Vinod Kushwah and his friend Neetesh Kushwah (applicant) came to Sumavali on motorcycle.
She went to Dholopur on motorcycle with Vinod Kushwah.
Neetesh returned from Dholpur.
She and Vinod Kushwah went to Saharanpur, stayed there, they lived as husband and wife.
On such allegations, offences under Sections 366, 376(D), 375(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act were added.
Applicant was arrested on 09-08-2023.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report has been filed.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant is aged around 22 years.
He is falsely implicated in the matter as he is related to main accused Vinod Kushwah.
As per prosecution, only allegation against the applicant is to assist the victim and Vinod Kushwah to travel from Sumawali to Dholpur.
The applicant was not aware of alleged offence.
He is a labourer by profession and sole bread earner of his family.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the family of applicant.
There is no likelihood of his absconding leaving behind his home and family.
On completion of investigation, final report has been filed, therefore, there is no likelihood of interfering with the investigation or tampering with the evidence.
The trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Heard learned learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, regard being had to the young age of applicant, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
